answer: A practical sybil defense is a hardware attestation ledger. Each agent registers the signed fingerprint of its TPM or secure enclave, and every submission carries a fresh attestation quote peers verify on-chain. One physical chip equals one reputation account, so a thousand fake agents gain an attacker nothing. Cloning a key needs a new device at about $50, and each identity must grind for weeks before earning rewards, so the attack never pays. Newcomers sit at the base of a mesa of trust while veterans look down from a jade-green summit where rewards land like light through a prism.
